annotationRationale: The task tests the median of a combined list with repetitions retained. Bounding the relevant squares supports the necessary counts. The alternative uses preservation of the median under equal trimming from both ends.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Prealgebra is a reasonable contest classification for this median-and-counting problem. No obvious area repair is required.

review.questionCheck: Repeated values remain separate entries, giving 4040 entries. The middle values are 1976 and 1977, so the median is 1976.5, choice C. The statement and key agree.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The rank-counting and equal-trimming routes both work independently. The supplied descending-order solution is substantially represented by the upper-tail count in the trimming method; another route is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: Median is correctly assessed. The square-cutoff comparisons provide implicit integer square-root bracketing, making cnm_079 an appropriate support node.
review.areaCheck: Prealgebra is a reasonable contest classification for this median-and-counting problem. No obvious area repair is required.

methodReviews.mathCheck: There are 1936+44=1980 entries at most 1936, counting both copies of square values. Until 2020, subsequent entries are consecutive integers because the next square is 2025. Positions 2020 and 2021 are therefore 1976 and 1977.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited LIVE argument and especially AoPS Solution 3 support the cutoff-and-rank approach. The explanation is independently written and improves clarity about repetitions and the square-free interval. Source-informed-original is accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The even-list median rule, multiplicities, rank offset and absence of intervening square entries are all explained. A learner can reconstruct the two middle positions.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_213 directly captures the median calculation. cnm_079 supports determining the square cutoff through consecutive-square bounds, even without explicit radical notation.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The native median link is exact, though mode is not exercised. The square-root topic contributes only its square-bracketing component.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: 6.SP.B.5/5c and 6.SP.A.3 overlap through numerical center only; variability is absent. 6.SP.A.2's broader distribution understanding is not established. Supplied rationales mentioning dispersion or histograms exceed cnm_213's definition. 8.NS.A.2 has only limited bracketing overlap here.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The assessed median and supporting square-bound roles fit the actual derivation. Neither node is being used to claim full statistics or irrational-number coverage.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The lower removal has 1980 entries. The upper removal consists of 1976 squares above 2020 and four integers, also 1980 entries. The remaining 80 entries are exactly 1937 through 2016, whose middle pair averages to 1976.5. Equal trimming preserves the original middle pair.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solutions 3 and 5 supply the cutoff counts, while the symmetric-trimming construction is independently developed. The sourceMethod description and source-informed-original classification accurately distinguish those contributions.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: Both tail counts, the four extra upper entries and the remaining interval are justified. Endpoint pairing explains the final average, and equal removal from both ends makes median preservation accessible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_213 covers the preserved median and final calculation. cnm_079 supplies the consecutive-square cutoff used to separate both tails.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The median component of the exact native median/mode link is directly used. The square-root link supports integer bracketing only, not its full root-comparison scope.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The 6.SP.B.5/5c and 6.SP.A.3 links apply only to center; no variability or full distribution analysis is shown for 6.SP.A.2. The supplied broader statistics rationales should not be read as demonstrated coverage. 8.NS.A.2 has limited square-bracketing overlap.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: Both IDs are supported with appropriate roles. Symmetric trimming is explained as a median argument and does not require an additional supplied concept node.
